title: An anchor (Hebrews 6:13–20)
hook: hope as an anchor of the soul, sure and steadfast
tomorrow: a priest-king walks into Genesis with bread and wine. who is he?

segments.voice: A week of letters: a grandmother and a mother, a finished race and a coat, God speaking in many ways, tested like us, a throne to walk up to, and obedience learned. Yesterday's line: learned through suffering.

Anyone who has slept on a boat knows the anchor doesn't stop the rocking. The waves keep coming all night. What the anchor stops is the drift: in the morning, the boat is still where it was. Hebrews reaches for that picture. But first it asks a strange question. People swear by something greater than themselves to settle an argument, and "an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife." So what does God swear by, when there's nothing greater?
screen: `THE ROCKING DOESN'T STOP.` → `THE DRIFT DOES.` → `WHAT DOES GOD SWEAR BY?`

segments.voice: The answer: "because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself." That's the promise to Abraham: "Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee." Said twice over, like a knot tied double. And Abraham, after he had patiently endured, obtained the promise. A promise and an oath, "two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie," given, the writer says, for those "who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us." Refugees, holding on. Then the picture: "Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast." The boat still rocks. It just doesn't drift. And then the image does something odd. This anchor doesn't drop into the sea. It goes up, "into that within the veil," behind the curtain of the sanctuary's innermost room, where, the writer says, Jesus has gone ahead as forerunner. The hope is fastened there, while the boat is still out on the water. Hope, in this letter, isn't a mood. It's a line with something solid on the other end. And the last verse calls that forerunner a high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec, a strange name the letter is about to explain.
screen: `HE SWARE BY HIMSELF.` · `TWO IMMUTABLE THINGS.` · `SURE AND STEDFAST.` · `WITHIN THE VEIL.` · then, large: `AN ANCHOR FOR THE SOUL.`

segments.voice: Pick up something with a little weight, a book, a bag, a full mug, and hold it in your lap with both hands. Close your eyes, and let your body sway slightly if it wants to while your hands keep the weight still: rocking, but not drifting. Stay with that until the sit ends, noticing the difference between the sway and the hold.
An anchor. Hebrews six: hope as an anchor of the soul, sure and steadfast, fastened within the veil, where the forerunner went first.
Your line: an anchor for the soul. The boat still rocks; it doesn't drift. That's the week.
